repos.description: Crop marketplace web app for farmers, buyers and admins (Node.js, Express, MySQL)
repos.readmeHtml:
CropVerse

A crop marketplace web app that connects farmers and buyers, with an admin who approves new accounts. Built as a DBMS Lab project.

Features

  • Signup with approval: new users verify with an emailed code, and an admin approves them before they can log in
  • Farmers: create, edit and delete crop listings, view a dashboard summary, see alerts, and submit crop disease reports
  • Buyers: browse the marketplace, purchase crops, view their dashboard, and view farmers' listings
  • Price trends: price chart pages for both farmers and buyers
  • Admin: review pending signups, approve users, and view all users

Tech stack

Part Technology
Frontend HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript
Backend Node.js, Express
Database MySQL (mysql2)
Auth JWT, bcryptjs
Email Nodemailer (SMTP)

Project structure

cropverse/
├── client/            # Frontend pages
│   ├── admin/         # Admin dashboard
│   ├── buyer/         # Buyer dashboard, marketplace, price chart
│   ├── farmer/        # Farmer dashboard, listings, disease report, price chart
│   ├── css/           # Styles
│   ├── js/            # Page scripts and API helper
│   └── *.html         # Landing, login, signup, verify pages
├── server/            # Backend API
│   ├── app.js         # Express routes
│   ├── db.js          # MySQL connection pool
│   ├── mailer.js      # Email sending
│   ├── schema.sql     # Database schema
│   └── .env.example   # Example environment settings
└── package.json

Getting started

You need: Node.js and MySQL installed.

  1. Install dependencies 
    npm run install:server
  2. Create the database. Run the schema in MySQL: 
    mysql -u root -p < server/schema.sql
  3. Set up your environment file. A server/.env with dummy placeholder values is included so the project runs out of the box. Change DB_PASS to match your own MySQL password, and use your own SMTP details if you want signup emails to send. For any real deployment, use a long random JWT_SECRET and never commit real secrets (server/.env.example shows the format).
  4. Start the API 
    npm start
    The API runs at http://localhost:4000. Check http://localhost:4000/api/health.
  5. Open the frontend. Serve the client/ folder with any static server (for example the VS Code "Live Server" extension) and open index.html.

If your API runs on a different address, set it in the browser console with localStorage.setItem("API_BASE", "http://your-address:port").

API overview

Area Endpoints
Auth POST /api/auth/signup, /api/auth/verify, /api/auth/login
Public GET /api/health, /api/crops, /api/listings, /api/price-trends
Farmer /api/farmer/listings, /api/farmer/my-listings, /api/farmer/disease-report, /api/farmer/alerts, /api/farmer/summary
Buyer /api/buyer/purchase, /api/buyer/dashboard, /api/farmers/:id/listings
Admin /api/admin/pending, /api/admin/users, /api/admin/approve
